Original Requirements: Generate a complete medium-size Python 3.10 repository architecture for: Flappy bird game. Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences): - build file: requirements.txt - runtime entry: Main.py - single test target: tests/test_main.py - test command: python -m pytest -q - keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed. Language/layout constraints: Keep Main.py as a thin entrypoint and put reusable modules in a lowercase snake_case package. List pytest in requirements.txt and avoid other external dependencies unless essential. Target Python 3.10 exactly: do not use typing.Self, StrEnum, exception groups, or other Python 3.11+ APIs. Design an acyclic import graph. Project-specific deterministic behavior and test contract: - Game begins in state "ready"; flap() in "ready" must atomically change the state to "running" and immediately apply config.flap_impulse, while flap() in "running" reapplies the impulse and flap() in "game_over" is a no-op - a running step first updates vertical velocity as clamp(vy + gravity, -max_vy, max_vy), then updates y by that velocity; therefore after an initial -8.0 flap and +0.5 gravity, one step exposes vy=-7.5 and a lower y - during each running step, move pipes, mark and score every unpassed pipe whose right edge is strictly left of bird_x exactly once, and only then remove off-screen pipes; passed remains observably true while that pipe remains in pipes_readonly() - make scoring independently testable with one precisely named pure helper and specify its exact signature in the Full API; unit-test that helper with a handcrafted pipe instead of waiting through a long Game loop - tests/test_main.py must contain only 2 to 4 short deterministic tests and must not advance dozens of ticks to test scoring - use only the canonical states "ready", "running", and "game_over" and repeat these state, flap, integration, scoring-order, and test rules in the Full API specification and every affected file task. Cross-cutting requirements: separate pure domain logic from runtime/UI/IO, deterministic tests, small files (<220 LOC), single canonical public API, no circular imports, no network/OS-specific behavior, and list all planned files/tasks.

Domain Reasoning: The game has three canonical states: ready, running, game_over
User action: flap() transitions ready->running atomically and applies impulse; flap() in running reapplies impulse; flap() in game_over is no-op
Physics: per-tick integration clamps vy after gravity then updates y
Pipes: move horizontally each tick; track pass state and remove only after scoring and off-screen check
Scoring: a pipe scores exactly once when its right edge is strictly left of bird_x; passed remains true while pipe is still listed
Collisions: hitting ground/ceiling or pipe sets state to game_over
Reset: restores initial state, clears or reinitializes entities deterministically
Pure helper for scoring to keep tests focused and deterministic
Domain Expectations: Bird position y and vertical velocity vy evolve deterministically with gravity and flap impulse
Game starts in ready; first flap atomically sets running and applies impulse immediately
Step order in running: apply gravity and clamp vy, update y, move pipes, score newly passed pipes, then remove off-screen pipes
Scoring helper pure function decides pass events based on pipe right edge vs bird_x
Pipes have gaps; collision occurs if bird y not within gap when overlapping pipe x-range
Game-over freezes physics and ignores flap until reset
pipes_readonly() exposes pipes including those already marked passed until removal
Configured parameters (gravity, flap_impulse, max_vy, speeds, dimensions) are validated
Product Goals: Deliver a clean, testable core game logic meeting the precise state, physics, and scoring rules
Provide a thin runtime demo that runs safely without loops or external dependencies
Ensure deterministic, concise tests that validate critical behaviors without UI coupling
User Stories: As a player, I want the first flap to start the game and boost the bird upward immediately.
As a player, I want gravity to pull the bird down predictably between flaps.
As a player, I want to earn a point exactly when I pass a pipe, not before or after.
As a player, I want the game to end on collision and allow me to reset cleanly.
As a developer, I want a pure helper to test scoring logic without running the full game loop.
Competitive Analysis: Original Flappy Bird: iconic, simple physics and timing-based challenge
Pygame Flappy Bird clones: accessible but often mix UI and logic tightly
Web-based clones: quick to play, limited testability and determinism
Teaching examples on GitHub: useful references but commonly lack clean separation of concerns

Requirement Analysis: We must design a Python 3.10 repository that cleanly separates domain logic from runtime and tests, strictly follows the protocol paths (requirements.txt, Main.py, tests/test_main.py), and provides deterministic behavior. The core must implement the three-state machine, flap semantics, physics integration order, pipe movement and collision, and scoring with a pure helper function. Imports must be acyclic, files small and focused, and the single test file must include 2–4 concise tests covering runtime wiring and core rules, including a direct unit test of the pure scoring helper to avoid long loops. Main.py should be a thin, non-interactive demo. The API must be canonical, stable, and fully documented for tests to consume.
Requirement Pool: Preserve protocol-required files exactly and keep Main.py thin
Implement core game mechanics: states (ready, running, game_over), flap semantics, gravity/velocity clamp, y update order
Implement pipes: movement, gap collision, pass detection and scoring order, off-screen removal
Expose a precisely named pure scoring helper with a fixed signature and unit-test it directly
Ensure deterministic, headless tests (2–4 concise tests) covering runtime wiring and representative rules
UI / UX / Interaction Design draft: Text-only demo in Main.py that constructs a Game, prints initial state, applies a flap, steps a few ticks, and prints state/score summary before exiting. No event loop, no rendering, and no input is required. All core logic resides in a package (e.g., flappy_core) with pure, deterministic functions and classes suitable for automated tests.
